claims.text:
26. conformal-sets

Target / packet: ai-conformal-sets · D2. Prerequisites: ai:calibration.

Nearest / distinct payoff: calibration → say-seventy-mean-it. A probability calibration statement is not a prediction set; this computes a calibration-score quantile and class membership, including empty/full outputs.

Finite primary model: Calibration nonconformity scores [.1,.2,.3], n=3; k=ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)). alpha=.25 gives k=3, q=.3. Candidate class scores 1-p for p=[.8,.15,.05] retain only A; uncertain p=[.4,.35,.25] yields empty set.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: alpha=.1 gives k=4>n: append infinite threshold, retain all classes. This calculation alone makes no marginal coverage claim; any theorem must state exchangeability and calibration protocol. Inclusive score<=q with tolerance.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict set size for uncertain probabilities; recall why empty and full sets are valid algorithm outputs under this quantile rule.

Required observable evidence: Show ordered calibration scores, threshold and membership; never substitute threshold for a 95% per-case confidence claim.

Source obligation: [Angelopoulos–Bates author tutorial](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.07511), acquired PDF body §1 split-conformal construction. The local three-score calculation uses the augmented infinite order statistic when k>n. No empirical or per-instance confidence promise; theorem wording must specify exchangeability and protocol before fact checking.
